about.text: Kashkaval is a type of cheese made from the milk of cows, sheep, goats, or a mixture thereof, popular in the Balkans, Turkey, and the Levant. In Hungary, kashkaval refers specifically to this type of cheese, whereas, in the rest of the Balkans, Turkey and the Levant, the term is often used to refer to all yellow cheeses. In English-language menus in Bulgaria, kashkaval is translated as 'yellow cheese'.

how.label: scald in brine
how.text: Kashkaval curd is cheddared until plastic, then sliced and scalded in hot salted water rather than plain water, kneaded and moulded into wheels; the brine scald salts the paste as it is stretched.

steps.note: The curd is cut to pea size.
The curd is cheddared until plastic.
The sliced curd is scalded in hot brine of 5–6 % salt.
